Route through cc10x: PLAN -> BUILD -> QA (Playwright) -> bug fixes until QA passes. Run fully autonomously; decide where decisions are needed; on a real blocker move to another part of the effort; stop only when done or fully blocked, then summarise work and gaps.

RD-3 APPROVED: workspace.last_activity_at is derived at read time from MAX(session.last_event_at), not written. Correct by construction, no new write path, and it stops a column that is always NULL being projected to the UI.

Reason: principle 5 - the unknown rate is counted and displayed, never hidden - and it is the headline metric section 12 puts on the fleet page. Capability preserved, U7 honoured, and most of test_fleet_page.py's assertions become body rewrites pointing at the new location rather than retirements.
Router correction: the frozen node-id count is 1480 (grep -c '::'), not 1482 (wc -l). The dispatch brief was wrong; the plan was right.

RD-4 DECIDED, reversing the design's file-layout row: escape.js is KEPT, byte-unchanged. UNREACHABLE_BY_DESIGN's reason string quotes the very test the retirement would remove, so deleting it either leaves a stale exemption citing a test that no longer collects or forces a third edit. One retirement, one post_milestone entry and one constant edit, all bought for tidiness. post_milestone drops 7 -> 6; retirements 17 -> 16.

Router correction to N2: reads.list_workspaces DOES have ORDER BY name (reads.py:102). The seeded 'Unassigned' sorts FIRST under BINARY collation (uppercase before lowercase), so all 8 list_workspaces()[0] sites read Unassigned instead of their own project. Deterministic, not flaky - it fails identically everywhere and cannot hide. The count is 8, not 10. The repair is selecting by name or captured id, never by position.

F13 DECIDED: tests/tools/test_render_check_args.py opens with pytest.importorskip('playwright'), and T0.1's exit asserts the suite still collects and passes without playwright installed. Same rule A6 states for esprima; marker deselection does not help because -m deselects after import.

Router: pass-2 findings are applied as a diff-scoped AMENDMENT rather than escalated. The two-pass fresh-review cap is spent, but all 15 findings carry named mechanical fixes and none is an owner decision. The amendment lane is uncapped and exists for exactly this case.

F6 pushback ACCEPTED: the planner's sink-to-module walk is right and the review's was not. Verified independently - 2520 renderLegend, 2858 BACK_BUTTON (flock.js); 2688 bylineMark, 2796/2814/2837 renderDetail (session.js, per D67); 3101 BACK_BUTTON_P (projects.js); 3617 panelHead (settings.js). T5.3 and T7.1 rewrite no sinks at all, so this removes work rather than moving it.

tools_projects.py is deliberately the one new module that is NOT pure: it runs the git probe, because git_common_dir is D48's binding key and a guessed value silently breaks session-to-project binding. The toolsurface->signals edge already exists at tools_m1.py:33.

esprima REPLACED by chromium in tools/js_syntax_check.py. esprima 4.0.1 is ES2017 and rejects ?., ??, class fields, #private, ||=, optional catch binding, import.meta and numeric separators - verified across 8 constructs - while being a Required Check in six later tasks that write three new modules. Chromium is the engine the code runs in, is already installed and already required. Cost, recorded not absorbed: no line number for a module compile error. A6 (no esprima under tests/) is retired.

T8.1 scope increases RATIFIED: Choice.number is int|None (the trust dialog's choices are unnumbered), Choice.selected exists (nowhere else to report which line carries the cursor), DecisionPrompt.kind exists (E17 requires the trust dialog be named so T8.2 refuses it by name rather than by sniffing its text). Each is forced by captured evidence, not preference.

The tests/golden claude-dir guard is NARROWED, not dropped: it excludes paths under the repository's own tree. This harness places agent worktrees at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/, so the bare '/.claude/' substring flagged 138 frozen captures. The clause is kept because it is the one that would catch ANOTHER user's config dir. Proven both ways with a four-case control.

A6 RETIRED in the plan: esprima replaced by chromium at Phase 0. The live form of that risk is playwright, which render_check.py imports at module level and pyproject.toml does not declare; pytest.importorskip guards it.

Phase 3 RATIFIED: delete_project is not registered, and test_delete_project_is_not_registered_and_the_reason_is_the_writer_thread asserts the absence so it goes red the moment someone wires it. A name a consumer can read but cannot call is worse than a gap that is stated.

Phase 3 RATIFIED: the three store-side refusal conventions are adapted to ONE record at the tool surface, not by changing store/. The reason is sharper than consistency - registry.py:69 turns any handler exception into GENERIC_ERROR = 'request failed', so a guard that RAISES reaches the page with no reason at all, and the reserved-project refusal is precisely the case a page must explain.

Phase 3 RATIFIED: T3.2's test lives in test_compose_m4.py rather than the plan's test_composition_root.py, which composes nothing (114 lines of AST rules, no store, host or SocketPlan). The seam is the plan's; only the file differs.

Phase 3 RATIFIED: add_repo resolves the repo's own root via repo_root - the same helper bind_cwd_to_repo uses - so a typed subdirectory cannot give one git_common_dir two repo rows under ux_repo_path.

T8.1 remfix RATIFIED: the degrade reason is NOT exposed on the return value. The interface stays DecisionPrompt | None so no caller can route on WHY a screen was unreadable; the branch tags are source comments read by the test through sys.settrace. Keeps degrade-never-guess a property rather than a protocol.

T8.1 remfix RATIFIED: the import-surface check calls the tree's shared _imports.module_imports from INSIDE the test body. A module-level AST walker would have been a sixth copy and would have needed an entry in test_one_definition_site.py's inventory - i.e. a duplicated walk laundered through an existing exception. No boundaries file was changed.

Phase 9 RATIFIED: #dlg-project and #dlg-delete are built by mountProjects() inside #page-projects rather than declared in index.html. A departure from T9.1's Consumes line, forced by the contract-first mode and better regardless - one reader, one contract.
Phase 9 RATIFIED: the first delete POST carries NO on_running key at all, not 'refuse'. A key that is absent cannot be edited out of the body; a key spelled 'refuse' can.
Phase 9 RATIFIED: the page confirms before it asks, because delete_project destroys on its first call and no dry-run route exists.

GAP 3 RESOLVED as set_project_description, a new verb rather than a widened rename_project. A verb called rename that edits a description is a verb whose name is wrong, and a two-field verb would have to invent absent-means-unchanged beside null-means-clear at the one surface where clearing is real intent. Named set_project_description rather than set_description because the registry is flat and a description is a field more than one thing has.

The 450-line cap gate is now GLOBBED rather than a hand-written tuple. tools_m1.py (574) and tools_master.py (505) have been OVER the cap since M1 and were never measured, because the tuple never named them; three more modules were never measured at all. Both are grandfathered BY NAME and PINNED AT THEIR CURRENT SIZE rather than exempted - so they cannot grow, and the exemption is visible rather than structural.

deferred_findings.finding: docs/design/ui-decisions.md says 'Everything in the prototype is textContent'. It is not: eight innerHTML assignments, all findings under unsafe_sinks. Scoped into T6.1; the sentence in ui-decisions.md still needs correcting.
docs/design/ui-decisions.md says one post_milestone declaration covers the redesign. Entries are per path; seven are needed. The sentence needs correcting.

Revision 4 states 19 sites for grep -rn '== 3\b' over the three migration test modules; that pattern returns 16 (union with EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION and [1,2,3] is 22). Conclusion unaffected - far more than the seven originally listed, and the plan carries the grep rather than a hand list. Fourth stated count in this plan to disagree with its source.

The plan's T0.1 exit criterion still greps for esprima, and a risk row still names it as an undeclared suite dependency. Both are now vacuous rather than wrong - the grep passes, nothing is red. Plan-owner edit.

js_syntax_check.py now needs playwright, as render_check.py already did. Neither is declared in pyproject.toml. The suite reaches the JS gate only by subprocess and the whole test file is behind pytest.importorskip, so a machine without playwright still collects and passes.

tools_projects.py is 408 lines against the 450 cap that now names it. delete_project plus its projection and three-branch handler is ~60-80 lines, so the authorised tools_projects.py + tools_projects_reads.py split is very likely required - and BOTH halves must be named on the cap line, or the split hides growth.
add_repo refusal completeness: absent, not-a-repo and bare are proved; an unreadable path, a submodule, and a filesystem vanishing mid-probe are not. get_project's session ordering is unpinned.

No capture exists of a dialog with more than three choices, a WRAPPED choice label, a subagent dialog, or the Tab-to-amend screen the permission footer advertises. A wrapped label is the likeliest breaker: a continuation line sits at the same label column and would be read as an extra choice, silently.

In 06-permission-dialog.ansi the command lines sit at column 3 - the choice column - and are kept out of the block only by the indent-1 question line above them. An engine drawing its question at column 3 would have it read as a choice. Structural residual; the standing reason the degrade rule must stay structural.

GAP 1 doomed: DeletePlan.doomed never reaches a consumer - the handler discards it and delete_outcome has no key. The refusal can say '2 running' and cannot say 'and 400 finished ones go with the project', which delete_outcome's own docstring says a person is owed. The page currently derives the count itself, a COPY of a store derivation - the thing that drifts.

GAP 2 killability: DeletePlan.running does not distinguish owned from attached, and the shipped kill answers no_pane for every attached session. So the page can offer a kill_sessions button that cannot succeed, with a refusal that does not say why.

GAP 3 description: no verb changes a description. create_project takes one; rename_project takes name only. A description is write-once at creation, so the Edit dialog renders the field inert with the reason rather than dropping typed text.

GAP 4 D60 unreachable: nothing answers WHICH projects hold this repo. D60 says a path may sit in more than one project and the row says so - but no read exposes it, and deriving it is an N+1 the projections were shaped to avoid. The page shows the path in full and invents nothing.

GAP 5 destructive-first-call: delete_project destroys on its first call when nothing is running, so a 'probe for the refusal' would destroy any idle project. The page confirms before it asks. A dry-run would close it properly.

The kill catch is `except Exception` precisely because nothing proves the shipped kill raises only RunnerRefusal. A kill that HANGS still blocks the verb - no timeout was added. And `killable` means the kill path has a pane to address, not that the kill will land; a stale handle is still a refusal, which is the blocking item's own case.
